judgments.comparative_verdict: Comparable: both reports hit all four expectations with precise file/line citations; Report 1 is marginally stronger on the legacy-billing removal, Report 2 marginally clearer on the migration-from-scratch point.

report_1.evidence: Line 2, `ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR = "true"` ... Delete the key entirely from the prod file. ... Line 3, `AUTH_RELAXED = "true"` ... Delete the key entirely. ... Line 4, `PRESET_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS = "qa@example.com:superadmin"` ... Delete the key entirely. ... Delete **both** keys from the prod file; do not just flip the flag ... Line 7, `LEGACY_BILLING_SECRET_ARN` ... delete the key

report_2.evidence: `infra/prod/app.auto.tfvars:2` — `ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR = "true"` ... Change to `"false"` or delete the key. ... `PRESET_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS` ... Remove the entry (set to empty) ... `SHADOW_SCORING_SINK` ... Either set it to `""` (which is what actually disables writing, per `config.py:21`)

report_1.evidence: The React app reads the API base URL from `import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL` **at build time** ... `npx vite build --mode staging` (line 14) — so the staging URL is what gets inlined ... The `deploy-prod` job ... then deploys "the same already-built digest to prod" ... production needs its own build (`.env.production` with the prod API URL, a `--mode production` build

report_2.evidence: Vite's `--mode staging` loads `frontend/.env.staging`, whose single line is `VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://staging-api.example.com` ... VITE_-prefixed variables are inlined into the built bundle at build time ... production users would load a frontend hard-wired to call `https://staging-api.example.com` ... one of the two has to change (per-environment builds, or runtime-injected API base URL)

report_1.evidence: **No migration step.** `docs/prod-runbook.md:6` claims "Database migrations are applied automatically during deploy," but ... the workflow contains no migration step at all ... the three migrations ... need an explicit first pass, manual or pipelined. "The pipeline succeeded" would not mean the schema exists.

report_2.evidence: **No database-migration step, contradicting the runbook.** `docs/prod-runbook.md:6` claims "Database migrations are applied automatically during deploy," but the workflow has no migration step ... The first release must bring a fresh production database from nothing through `0001_base`, `0002_tenants`, and `0003_billing` ... as things stand nothing will do that.

report_1.evidence: **Production, as authored:** `infra/prod/main.tf:3` passes the **identical staging condition** ... any job running in the *staging* environment **would** satisfy the prod role's trust condition, letting staging-scoped CI assume production deploy credentials. The fix is `oidc_sub_condition = "repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:production"`

report_2.evidence: `infra/prod/main.tf:3` — unedited from the staging copy — trusts `repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:staging` ... any job running in the *staging* GitHub environment **can** assume the production deploy role ... Change to `repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:production`.
